title: Air humidity and dew point
prompt:
Meteorology. Use the Magnus formula for the saturation vapour pressure over water, e_s(T) = 6.112·exp(17.62·T / (243.12 + T)) hPa (T in °C); relative humidity RH = 100·e / e_s(T); the dew point is the temperature at which e_s equals the actual vapour pressure e; the mixing ratio is w = 622·e / (p − e) g/kg; the cloud-base height is estimated as 125 m per °C of the difference between temperature and dew point. Find the requested quantity in each of the following 23 independent situations:
1. air temperature 15.2 °C, relative humidity 21 %; dew point in °C.
2. air temperature -3.6 °C, relative humidity 57 %; dew point in °C.
3. air temperature -13.0 °C, relative humidity 66 %, pressure 820 hPa; water-vapour mixing ratio in g/kg.
4. air temperature -13.2 °C, dew point -29.7 °C; relative humidity in %.
5. air temperature 20.1 °C, relative humidity 26 %; dew point in °C.
6. air temperature 20.5 °C, relative humidity 55 %, pressure 1030 hPa; water-vapour mixing ratio in g/kg.
7. air temperature -0.4 °C, relative humidity 51 %, pressure 871 hPa; water-vapour mixing ratio in g/kg.
8. air temperature 29.3 °C, relative humidity 43 %, pressure 1003 hPa; water-vapour mixing ratio in g/kg.
9. air temperature 8.1 °C, relative humidity 36 %; estimated cloud-base height in m.
10. air temperature -7.3 °C, relative humidity 48 %; estimated cloud-base height in m.
11. air temperature 6.1 °C, relative humidity 50 %; dew point in °C.
12. air temperature 20.7 °C, relative humidity 27 %, pressure 887 hPa; water-vapour mixing ratio in g/kg.
13. air temperature 27.3 °C, relative humidity 57 %, pressure 927 hPa; water-vapour mixing ratio in g/kg.
14. air temperature -13.1 °C, dew point -33.8 °C; relative humidity in %.
15. air temperature 4.0 °C, dew point 1.8 °C; relative humidity in %.
16. air temperature 2.6 °C, relative humidity 43 %, pressure 892 hPa; water-vapour mixing ratio in g/kg.
17. air temperature 19.3 °C, relative humidity 54 %, pressure 758 hPa; water-vapour mixing ratio in g/kg.
18. air temperature 7.4 °C, dew point -10.2 °C; relative humidity in %.
19. air temperature -5.6 °C, relative humidity 64 %; estimated cloud-base height in m.
20. air temperature 10.7 °C, relative humidity 39 %; dew point in °C.
21. air temperature 35.6 °C, relative humidity 82 %; estimated cloud-base height in m.
22. air temperature 12.8 °C, relative humidity 15 %, pressure 997 hPa; water-vapour mixing ratio in g/kg.
23. air temperature 9.2 °C, relative humidity 42 %; estimated cloud-base height in m.

Give the 23 requested values, each with 4 significant figures, in the order listed, as plain decimal numbers separated by commas.

Think it through, then finish with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <your answer>`.

title: Drug concentration after repeated doses
prompt:
Pharmacokinetics, one-compartment model with instantaneous intravenous bolus doses and first-order elimination (each dose instantly raises the concentration by dose / volume; concentrations from separate doses add up). In each of the following 10 independent regimens find the requested concentration:
1. a dose of 600 mg every 24 h, 3 doses in total starting at t = 0; volume of distribution 64 L, elimination half-life 1.2 h; plasma concentration in mg/L at t = 48.9 h.
2. a dose of 590 mg every 12 h, 7 doses in total starting at t = 0; volume of distribution 16 L, elimination half-life 14.9 h; plasma concentration in mg/L at t = 26.4 h.
3. a dose of 340 mg every 4 h, 6 doses in total starting at t = 0; volume of distribution 36 L, elimination half-life 13.5 h; plasma concentration in mg/L at t = 5.5 h.
4. a dose of 670 mg every 6 h, 8 doses in total starting at t = 0; volume of distribution 16 L, elimination half-life 8.7 h; plasma concentration in mg/L at t = 30.6 h.
5. a dose of 190 mg every 12 h, 3 doses in total starting at t = 0; volume of distribution 40 L, elimination half-life 20.9 h; plasma concentration in mg/L at t = 41.7 h.
6. a dose of 330 mg every 4 h, 5 doses in total starting at t = 0; volume of distribution 66 L, elimination half-life 13.1 h; plasma concentration in mg/L at t = 32.9 h.
7. a dose of 730 mg every 8 h, 8 doses in total starting at t = 0; volume of distribution 66 L, elimination half-life 10.8 h; plasma concentration in mg/L at t = 53.0 h.
8. a dose of 180 mg every 12 h, 3 doses in total starting at t = 0; volume of distribution 40 L, elimination half-life 19.1 h; plasma concentration in mg/L at t = 53.2 h.
9. a dose of 250 mg every 8 h, 4 doses in total starting at t = 0; volume of distribution 17 L, elimination half-life 5.1 h; plasma concentration in mg/L at t = 13.8 h.
10. a dose of 200 mg every 24 h, 6 doses in total starting at t = 0; volume of distribution 22 L, elimination half-life 22.2 h; plasma concentration in mg/L at t = 107.7 h.

Give the 10 requested values, each with 4 significant figures, in the order listed, as plain decimal numbers separated by commas.

Think it through, then finish with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <your answer>`.

title: Absorbing Markov chain
prompt:
A token moves on the states S1, …, S11, W and L. Each step it moves from its current state according to the transition probabilities below (a move to the same state is allowed); W and L are absorbing (the token stays there forever).
from S1: to S1 with probability 0.1, to S5 with probability 0.2, to S8 with probability 0.5, to L with probability 0.2
from S2: to S2 with probability 0.2, to S5 with probability 0.5, to W with probability 0.3
from S3: to S5 with probability 0.2, to S7 with probability 0.4, to W with probability 0.1, to L with probability 0.3
from S4: to S4 with probability 0.2, to S7 with probability 0.8
from S5: to S3 with probability 0.2, to S6 with probability 0.3, to S9 with probability 0.2, to L with probability 0.3
from S6: to S3 with probability 0.4, to L with probability 0.6
from S7: to S6 with probability 0.3, to L with probability 0.7
from S8: to S3 with probability 0.4, to L with probability 0.6
from S9: to S5 with probability 0.1, to S8 with probability 0.1, to S10 with probability 0.3, to W with probability 0.5
from S10: to S9 with probability 0.4, to S11 with probability 0.6
from S11: to S11 with probability 0.2, to W with probability 0.3, to L with probability 0.5

The token starts in S1. Find (1) the probability that it is eventually absorbed in W and (2) the expected number of steps until it is absorbed (in W or L). Give the 2 values, each with 4 significant figures, as plain decimal numbers separated by commas.

Think it through, then finish with a final line of the form `ANSWER: <your answer>`.
